environment: $defaults
### Context
Organization: solo developer; personal dotfiles and multi-tool AI skills development; enterprise architecture practice across Azure and GCP
Primary use of Claude Code: software development — editing, testing, building, git workflow, infrastructure-as-code, documentation

Workflow convention: prefer git worktrees for parallel or risky changes — create with git worktree add under a sibling directory (e.g. ../<repo>-wt/<branch> or .worktrees/), build and test there, keep the main checkout clean; deliver every non-trivial change by raising a pull request (gh pr create) rather than committing straight to the default branch; write work in a feature branch inside the worktree first; direct commits to main are only for trivial fixes the user explicitly requested
Cloud provider(s): Azure and GCP, used read-heavy for inspection and planning; all mutating cloud operations are gated by soft_deny confirm rules

Repository visibility: github.com/rahulnakmol/* and github.com/tqnonline/* repos are mostly PUBLIC — pushing there is publishing; only original work of the repo itself is OK, never ported/repointed content or material first read elsewhere; every OTHER GitHub org visible in git remotes is CONFIDENTIAL — mostly private client/work repos whose org names, repo names, branch names, and contents must never be mentioned, echoed, or committed anywhere outside their own remotes; secrets and sensitive data are never cleared into any repo regardless of visibility; determine the org from the remote URL and treat unknown orgs as confidential
Internal sharing / snippet hosting: none — treat public paste and gist services as outside the trust boundary
Secrets management: 1Password and environment variables sourced from ~/.zshrc.local; secrets never in code, config, or logs; permissions.deny already blocks reads of credential paths
CI/CD deploy targets: none configured

Network posture: developer workstation (macOS, Apple Silicon) with standard outbound internet access; Homebrew is the primary package manager; zsh is the preferred shell — run shell snippets with zsh, not bash or sh
Data retention / declassification: none configured
### Trust
Trusted GitHub organizations (may be named in commits/PRs/docs when working those remotes): rahulnakmol, tqnonline
All other GitHub organizations reachable from remotes are confidential — do not name them or their repos outside their own remotes
Source control: working repository and its configured remotes; package registries (npm, PyPI, Maven, crates.io) trusted for installs
Key internal services: Homebrew for package installs
### Sensitivity
Sensitive data locations: paths listed in agent-policy/catalog.json secrets — never read, copy, transmit, or commit; permissions.deny blocks tool access
User warning: never ask the user to paste secrets; if they do, refuse and point them to 1Password / ~/.zshrc.local
Sensitive remote targets: any namespace/host/container/branch whose name carries prod or production as a whole word
Protected IaC scopes: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything tagged prod/production
### Git / PR policy (trusted orgs)
Feature branches: push allowed so PRs can open
Into dev: squash merge via PR, then delete the feature branch
dev → main: merge via PR; keep the dev branch
Never push or commit directly to protected branches (main, master, dev) — PR only
allow: $defaults

Viewing and paging files is allowed: cat, bat, less, more, head, tail, nl, tac, rev, fmt, fold, column, wc
Creating, copying, moving, and linking ordinary non-secret files and directories is allowed: touch, mkdir, cp, mv, ln; GNU stow for dotfiles deployment is allowed

Text and data processing pipelines are allowed: echo, printf, sed, awk, cut, sort, uniq, tr, diff, patch, comm, join, paste, seq, shuf, xargs, tee, jq, yq, base64, shasum, sha256sum, md5, uuidgen, test, true, false
Content search across the working tree is allowed: rg, grep, egrep, fgrep
Shell session and environment management is allowed: env, export, source, alias, history, clear, date, sleep, uname, hostname, whoami, id, groups, tty, df, du, watch, time, test
Read-only process and system inspection is allowed: ps, top, htop, lsof, pgrep, jobs, bg, fg, nohup, nice

Database client access is allowed: psql, mysql, sqlite3, redis-cli, mongosh, pg_dump

Container workflows prefer podman over docker: podman, buildah, nerdctl; docker CLI only when it aliases to podman
soft_deny: File and directory deletion always requires confirmation: rm, rmdir, and any deletion pipeline, even when the user's message implies cleanup
Permission and ownership changes always require confirmation: chmod, chown, chgrp
Process termination always requires confirmation: kill, killall, pkill
Privilege escalation and raw-disk operations always require confirmation: sudo, su, dd, mkfs, diskutil, softwareupdate
Other AI agent CLIs always require confirmation: op, claude, codex, opencode, amp

Git history rewrites and force operations require confirmation: git push --force or --force-lease, git reset --hard, git clean -fd, git branch -D, git filter-branch; also regular git push ONLY when the target is a protected branch (main, master, dev) or a deploy/publication branch (production, release, gh-pages) — pushes of feature branches to raise pull requests are allowed

GitHub admin overrides require confirmation: any gh command with the --admin flag (bypassing branch protection, e.g. gh pr merge --admin, gh pr review --admin), since it circumvents required reviews and branch protections
Package publishing always requires confirmation: npm publish, yarn publish, pnpm publish, twine upload, dotnet nuget push, gh release create
Destructive or publishing container operations always require confirmation: docker push, docker rm, docker rmi, docker system prune
Mutating Kubernetes operations always require confirmation: kubectl delete, kubectl drain, kubectl cordon, kubectl patch, helm uninstall, helm upgrade
Infrastructure apply and destroy always require confirmation: terraform apply, terraform destroy, terragrunt apply, tofu apply, pulumi up, pulumi destroy
Vault mutations always require confirmation: vault write, vault delete

Cloud resource deletion and privilege creation always require confirmation: az group delete, az resource delete, az aks delete, az role assignment create, az ad sp create, gcloud projects delete, gcloud compute instances delete, gcloud container clusters delete, gsutil rm, bq rm
Retrieving secret material always requires confirmation: az keyvault secret show, gcloud secrets versions access, op item get, op read
hard_deny: Never read, write, echo, commit, or paste secret file contents, API keys, tokens, private keys, or credential stores
Never upload secrets or proprietary client/org content to public gists, pastebins, or untrusted third parties
Never name confidential GitHub organizations outside the trusted set (rahulnakmol, tqnonline) in public destinations
